current_mechanisms.name: Q/K private steering
current_mechanisms.difference: Current private factor/scoring directions change score/value access and conditional kernels while retaining slow parameter sharing across complete member trajectories. NeuroTrails instead partially unties full late blocks and sparsifies connections. It does not substitute for the Q/K reversibility/function-family test.

current_mechanisms.name: Graph transport/private incidence factors
current_mechanisms.difference: Current map-to-normalized-transport capacity and operator-response diversity leave original feature/head/slow maps shared. NeuroTrails changes neural connection topology and late weight ownership, not graph relation transports or gauge-invariant operator actions.

current_mechanisms.name: Source-supply
current_mechanisms.difference: Current own joint training receives a guarded private correction based on recipient factual/probe credit. NeuroTrails uses ordinary mean member supervision and no raw source removal, source responsibilities, U/D specificity or signed probe derivative.

closest_saved_published_methods.name: HGEN
closest_saved_published_methods.fact: Separate semantic/meta-path graph learners, fused task loss and Gram penalty. Already addresses different graph evidence using independently parameterized learners; no current shared-member competence theorem.

closest_saved_published_methods.name: GNCL
closest_saved_published_methods.fact: Own/aggregate task-risk mixtures already train for committee utility. NeuroTrails inspected objective is the mean-own end of that family; a new scalar diversity coefficient would add no new mechanism.

closest_saved_published_methods.name: SuGAr
closest_saved_published_methods.fact: Independent GNNs learn diverse graph/edge selectors. Neural sparse-mask exploration differs from graph-edge selection, but both are established selection/diversification ingredients and neither guarantees useful complementarity.

closest_saved_published_methods.name: FoRDE
closest_saved_published_methods.fact: Repulsion of normalized true-label input-logprob gradients is classifier-facing response diversity. It does not remove a shared parameter-capacity restriction or show actual shared-step harm.

closest_saved_published_methods.name: SuperWeights and partial-sharing/fission ensembles
closest_saved_published_methods.fact: Saved source already learns joint parameter allocation from gradient conflict. NeuroTrails combines known partial sharing and dynamic sparsity; this is a useful attributed capacity/topology control, not new learned sharing.

diagnostic_separation: Capacity deficiency: actual member function family/private support cannot express useful repairs. More raw parameters or differing masks do not diagnose it.

Optimization interference: realized native total step harms a member after its own private progress is accounted for. Pairwise shared-gradient cosine is not sufficient, especially with Adam moments/finite steps.

Auxiliary-induced weakness: diversity/source loss changes cause harm even when native own-only shared model remains competent. Must isolate objective and ownership before adding capacity/optimizer remedies.
scope_limit: Only saved conceptual/current-proposal summaries were used. Incidental previously saved TabM/contrastive summaries and FoRDE engineering receipt details were exposed; no raw outcome, checkpoint, prediction or dataset file was opened or used for a new empirical conclusion.
